answer: The most convincing sybil defense is on-ledger slashing of verifiers: every countersignature on an invalid transaction stakes real value, and anyone can submit proof of a bad countersign, burning the verifier's bond on-chain. If the slash exceeds a full epoch of rewards plus fees, random identity roulette beats buying votes, so a relic pool of sockpuppets loses money faster than any zenith of fake verifiers can earn, and each jetty of new identities must post unforgeable stake, not just cheap accounts.
